rules.label: Subject-verb agreement
rules.why: With he / she / it the verb takes -s, even in the negative: 'He doesn't like it'.

rules.label: Subject-verb agreement
rules.why: With I / we / you / they the verb has no -s: 'They don't like it'.

rules.label: Subject-verb agreement
rules.why: 'I' takes 'am' in the present and 'was' in the past: 'I am', 'I was' - never 'I is' or 'I are'.

rules.label: Subject-verb agreement
rules.why: With we / they / you the plural verb is 'are', never 'is'.

rules.label: Subject-verb agreement
rules.why: With we / they / you the past plural is 'were', never 'was'.

rules.label: Subject-verb agreement
rules.why: 'I' takes 'was' in the past, never 'were'.

rules.label: Subject-verb agreement
rules.why: With he / she / it the verb is 'has', never 'have'.

rules.label: Subject-verb agreement
rules.why: With I / we / they / you the verb is 'have', never 'has'.

rules.label: Present perfect needs a participle
rules.why: After have / has / been the verb must be the past participle: 'I have gone', not 'I have went'.

rules.label: Past tense needs the base verb
rules.why: After don't / doesn't / didn't the verb goes back to its base form: 'I didn't go', not 'I didn't went'.

rules.label: Double comparison
rules.why: Do not use 'more' with a word that is already comparative: 'more better' becomes 'better'.

rules.label: Double superlative
rules.why: 'Most' doubles the superlative: 'most best' becomes 'the best'.

rules.label: Modal verb never takes to
rules.why: Modal verbs stand alone: 'can go', 'must go' - never 'can to go'.

rules.label: Modal verb never takes to
rules.why: A modal verb takes the base form directly - there is nothing after the 'to' here.

rules.label: Wrong word
rules.why: 'Agree' is a verb. Say 'I agree' or 'I am in agreement with you'.

rules.label: Extra preposition
rules.why: 'Discuss' is transitive and takes no 'about': 'discuss the plan'.

rules.label: Explain needs to me
rules.why: 'Explain' takes the thing first, then the person: 'explain it to me'.

rules.label: Uncountable noun
rules.why: 'Advice' has no plural. Say 'a piece of advice'.

rules.label: Uncountable noun
rules.why: This noun has no plural in English: 'information', 'advice', 'equipment'.

rules.label: Wrong idiom
rules.why: The phrase is 'regardless of' or 'in spite of'.

rules.label: Wrong idiom
rules.why: 'Despite' takes no 'of': 'despite the rain'.

rules.label: Wrong preposition
rules.why: For a duration use 'for': 'for three years'. Use 'since' with a point in time: 'since 2020'.

rules.label: Wrong preposition
rules.why: The set phrase is 'interested in something'.

rules.label: Wrong preposition
rules.why: Always 'depend on' - never 'depend of'.

rules.label: Wrong preposition
rules.why: 'Marry' takes no preposition: 'I married Ali'.

rules.label: Wrong preposition
rules.why: After 'wait' use 'to' + base verb: 'waiting to see'.

rules.label: Correct preposition
rules.why: Good - keep 'depend on' and 'concentrate on'.

rules.label: Repetition
rules.why: One 'same' is enough.

rules.label: Doubled word
rules.why: The word is repeated - a slip of the keyboard or the tongue.

rules.label: Redundant
rules.why: 'Age' is not needed after 'years old'.

rules.label: Fixed expression
rules.why: The set phrase is 'in conclusion', no article.

rules.label: Redundant
rules.why: 'By the time' already means 'when'.

rules.label: Double determiner
rules.why: Choose one: 'every student' or 'each student'.

rules.label: Over-specified
rules.why: 'Both' already means two: 'both students'.

rules.label: Wrong word
rules.why: The verb is 'affect', the noun is 'effect': 'the effect of the rain'.

rules.label: Missing apostrophe
rules.why: 'You're welcome' and 'you're right' use the contraction 'you are'.

rules.label: Possessive vs contraction
rules.why: 'Its' shows possession; 'it's' means 'it is' or 'it has'.

rules.label: Double comparison
rules.why: Use one comparative only: 'more than', not 'more than more'.

rules.label: Missing auxiliary
rules.why: The negative needs a helper verb: 'I don't understand', never 'I no understand'.

rules.label: Wrong word order
rules.why: With I / we / they the progressive is am / are + V-ing: 'I am learning'.

rules.label: Third person singular -s
rules.why: With he / she / it the present simple verb takes -s: 'He goes to school'.

rules.label: Wrong word
rules.why: 'Agree' is a verb: 'I agree with you', not 'I am agree'.

rules.label: Duration phrase
rules.why: 'for' goes before the duration: 'for three years'.

rules.label: Age takes be, not have
rules.why: English is the other way round from «۲۰ سال دارم»: the person is the age. 'I am 20 years old'.

rules.label: Age takes be, not has
rules.why: «۲۰ سال دارد» becomes 'He is 20', not 'He has 20 years'.

rules.label: Asking age
rules.why: Age is asked with 'How old', not 'How much'. «چند سالت است؟» → 'How old are you?'

rules.label: Married takes to
rules.why: 'Marry' and 'be married' take 'to' in English, where Persian uses «با».

rules.label: Base verb after did
rules.why: 'Did' already carries the past, so the next verb stays in its base form: 'did you go', not 'did you went'.

rules.label: Naming things
rules.why: English asks what we call a thing, not how: «این را چه مینامید؟» → 'What do you call this?'

rules.label: Photos are of
rules.why: You take a photo **of** something. 'From' comes from «عکس گرفتن از».

rules.label: Photos are taken
rules.why: English takes photographs; it does not make them, even though Persian «عکس گرفتن» uses a verb closer to taking than making.

rules.label: Lights are turned on
rules.why: «چراغ را روشن کن» becomes 'turn the light on' — devices are turned on, not opened.

rules.label: Lights are turned off
rules.why: «چراغ را خاموش کن» becomes 'turn the light off'. 'Close' is for doors and books.

rules.label: Say needs to
rules.why: 'Tell' takes a person bare — 'tell me' — but 'say' needs 'to': 'say it to me'.

rules.label: Let's takes no to
rules.why: 'Let's' already contains the verb: 'let's go', never 'let's to go'.

rules.label: Suggest takes that
rules.why: 'Suggest' does not take an object + to-infinitive in English: 'suggest that you go' or 'suggest going'.

rules.label: Recommend needs to
rules.why: 'Recommend' and 'describe' need 'to' before the person: 'recommend it to me'.

rules.label: Illness takes a
rules.why: «سرما خوردم» is 'I have a cold' — the illness is countable here, so it needs 'a'.

rules.label: Every day is two words
rules.why: 'Everyday' is an adjective ('everyday English'). When it answers *when*, it is two words: 'I practise every day'.

rules.label: Home takes no to
rules.why: 'Home' works like 'there' and 'abroad' — no preposition: 'I'm going home'.

rules.label: Last night, no in
rules.why: 'Last night' and 'last week' take no preposition in English, where Persian has «دیشب»/«هفتهٔ پیش» as single words.

rules.label: Since is a point in time
rules.why: 'Since' marks when something started (since 2020). A length of time takes 'for' (for three years).

rules.label: Reply needs to
rules.why: 'Reply' and 'answer' take the person with 'to' when a verb follows: 'reply to me'.

rules.label: Listen needs to
rules.why: 'Listen' takes 'to' before the person or thing: 'listen to me'. ('Hear' takes none.)

rules.label: Wait needs for
rules.why: 'Wait for someone' — the person is not the direct object in English.

rules.label: Arrive at, not to
rules.why: You arrive **at** a place or **in** a city. 'Arrive to' comes straight from «رسیدن به».

rules.label: Mistakes are made
rules.why: English makes mistakes and does favours — the reverse of Persian «اشتباه کردن».

rules.label: Interested, not interesting
rules.why: People are **interested**; things are **interesting**. «به تاریخ علاقه دارم» → 'I am interested in history'.

rules.label: Duration needs the perfect
rules.why: A stretch of time that started in the past and continues now takes the perfect: 'I have been living here for three years'.

rules.label: Mistakes are made — does
rules.why: English *makes* mistakes, not «does» them: 'he makes a mistake'.

rules.label: Mistakes are made — do
rules.why: 'Make a mistake' is the fixed collocation, so the auxiliary keeps 'do' and the verb becomes 'make'.

rules.label: Mistakes are made — continuous
rules.why: The -ing form is 'making a mistake' — «دارم اشتباه می‌کنم» maps to 'I'm making a mistake'.
